description: Use when someone asks how many memecoins launched on pump.fun, what memecoin launchpads earned in fees, how much traded on Kalshi and Polymarket, how many Americans filed first jobless claims, how many paid calls wallets made over x402 on Base and what each cost, or what the US jobs number, unemployment rate, CPI or core CPI was when first published, before the Bureau of Labor Statistics revised it. Tickerz reads each as an index against its own normal (daily, weekly for LAYOFFS, monthly for JOBS, UNEMP, CPI and CORECPI), each reading timestamped in Bitcoin so it cannot be changed afterward. Every Tickerz Index: what it counts, its source, the newest day, the Activity score and signed z of the newest complete day, and the last 30 complete days as period, value and band. GIGS counts paid x402 calls settled on Base; WAGE is dollars per call, the payer-balanced median. WAGE days carry p25 and p75, the 25th and 75th percentiles in dollars per call, where the store has them. GIGS and WAGE complete days carry thin and sampled_payers: thin is true when sampled paying wallets are under 70% of the median of the 28 complete days before that day, once 14 earlier days are on file, and the level stays. Fewer earlier days is not marked. For a finished period read latest_complete. latest is the newest period on file; when it has provisional true it is a partial UTC day still counting, marked partial_day true, and its change_pct (also given as partial_change_pct) compares that partial day with a full one, so it is not a full-day change. Some sources land late (jobless claims about ten days after the week ends, Chicago crime over about a week), so latest_complete can be days behind today. Same data as GET /api/indices. A source whose terms keep its levels out of the API is served with its score and bands only.
